Here's the formula you should place in cell U108:

```excel
=SUMIF(U:U, "Outstanding", S:S)
```

This formula works as follows:
- `U:U`: This is the range that Excel will search for the criterion, in this case, every cell in column U.
- `"Outstanding"`: This is the criterion Excel will search for within the specified range.
- `S:S`: This is the sum range; for each row where the criterion is met in column U, the corresponding cell in column S will be included in the sum.

Make sure that in Excel 2003, your data range doesn't extend beyond the row limit of the application, which is 65,536 rows. If your range is more limited (e.g., it only goes down to row 500), you can specify the actual range to improve performance like so:

```excel

stream_episodes.pos:
To remove duplicate entries from a column in Excel 2003, you can use the built-in "Advanced Filter" feature. Here's how you can do it:

1. Select the column that contains the data you want to remove duplicates from.

2. Go to the "Data" menu and click on "Filter" -> "Advanced Filter".

3. In the "Advanced Filter" dialog box, select the "Copy to another location" option.

4. In the "Copy to" field, specify a destination range where you want the unique values to be copied. For example, you can choose an empty column adjacent to the original column.

5. Ensure that the "Unique records only" checkbox is checked.

6. Click "OK".

7. Excel will copy only the unique values from the selected column to the destination range you specified.

8. Now, you can remove the original column if you no longer need it.

By following these steps, you can remove duplicate entries from a column in Excel 2003 using the Advanced Filter feature. The unique values will be copied to a separate location, allowing you to easily identify and work with them.
stream_episodes.neg:
To convert columns to text in Excel 2003, you can use the CONCATENATE function or the ampersand (&) operator. Here's how you can do it:

1. Assuming you have columns A, B, and C that you want to combine into a single text in column D:

     A       |     B      |    C     |     D
 ----------------------------------------------
    Text 1  |   Text 2  |  Text 3 |  Result

2. In cell D1, enter the following formula:

   =A1&B1&C1

   This formula combines the text in cells A1, B1, and C1 using the ampersand operator.

3. Press Enter to get the combined text in cell D1.

4. Drag the formula down in column D to fill the rest of the cells with the combined text.

5. Now, you can copy the combined text in column D and paste it as values (right-click -> Paste Special -> Values) to remove the formula and keep only the combined text.

By following these steps, you can convert columns to text in Excel 2003 using the CONCATENATE function or the ampersand (&) operator.
